newsitem.title: CHINA: China stocks to consolidate on warning.
newsitem.headline: China stocks to consolidate on warning.

text.p: The bull run on China's stock markets is likely to slow over the next few weeks largely due to persistent rumours that the securities authorities are planning new anti-speculative measures, analysts said on Sunday.
Stock prices in Shanghai and Shenzhen have risen an average of more than 40 percent since the beginning of the year amid beliefs among investors that the economy was in good shape.
Beijing's regulators are unhappy about the fast rise and have issued a number of warnings in the official press in the past week against market volatility.
"The risks are growing due to the possibility of policy changes, with the official papers warning investors about overheating on the markets," said an analyst with a major Chinese brokerage.

"There are widespread rumours including some saying the securities authorities have convened a meeting of brokerages to ask them cool down trading," said a broker. "Many investors expect the central government to take some sort of action."
One rumour is that Beijing is considering replacing the current T+1 or next-day settlement system with T+2 or third-day settlement system to reduce the flow of speculative funds, brokers said.
Investors are mostly sticking to the sidelines, waiting to see what emerges from the warnings and the rumours.

"Consolidation will be the major trend over the next month," said a Shanghai-based stock analyst with Guangfa Securities. "Price movements will largely be in line with whatever happens on the policy front."
But analysts said substantially-improved market fundamentals over the past year will limit the potential for a fall.
They say there is a fundamental difference in psychology between the speculative stock "stir-frying" of late last year and the more steady gains of recent months.
"Official efforts to cool down the markets will at most push the index down 10 percent," said a Shenzhen-based analyst with J & A Securities.
"Official measures should not effect the indices too much because the stock markets have been trading sensibly on an improvement in the fundamentals," said another Shenzhen-based analyst.
Shanghai's foreign currency B share index, which closed on Friday at 73.32 points, is likely to move around the 70-point level over the next month or so, analysts predicted.
The Shanghai domestic A share index, which ended Friday at 1,340.593, will probably consolidate around the 1,300 mark, they said.

Shenzhen's B share index, which ended last week at 157.34 points, will move around 150-160 points, while the A share index was at 453.62 by Friday's close and could hit a low of 410 points, brokers said.
"Investors are likely to stay on the sidelines for a few weeks to see if any concrete measures are introduced to cool the markets down," said one analyst.

Beijing announced on Thursday it would soon allow non-listed state firms to issue four billion yuan worth of convertible bonds, which analysts said was partly an effort to divert funds from the stock markets and reduce speculative trading.
"The CB issue is one of the means by which the administration will adjust the stock secondary markets," the China Securities newspaper said.
